name: BitPay
technique: server hot wallet breach; social engineering
classificationNote: Classified by TypeSafe jev-1.13.0 (confidence 0.97). Replaced keyword guess "key-compromise".
rootCause: The attacker spearphished the CFO (with what looks to be a compromised email / server of someone else, this is unclear) and successfully acquired his credentials with a phishing page. These credentials were then used to communicate with the CEO and request multiple large transfers to the amount of $1.8 Million USD. A customer pointed out the fraud. Below is the root cause as pointed out by court documents. On or about December 11, 2014, Bryan Krohn, the CFO of Bitpay, received an email from someone purporting to be David Bailey of yBitcoin (a digital currency publication) requesting Mr. Krohn comment on a bitcoin industry document.
